long_biography.plain_text:
Philippe Rousselet built Vendôme as a transatlantic production and financing group after learning the American studio system at Warner Bros. He created a French production company in the 1990s, later established Vendôme Pictures in Los Angeles and assembled bank and private-equity backing for an international film slate.

An investment in Jerico Films brought La Famille Bélier into the group. Rousselet chose to produce its American adaptation, CODA, rather than license the story; the film won the Academy Award for Best Picture. He continues to chair Vendôme and leads an English-language production venture formed with Pathé and Merit France.

Philippe Rousselet, a renowned French film producer at the age of 55, has gained recognition for his remarkable contributions to the film industry. Among his notable works is the 2010 movie "Women on the 6th Floor," which he produced. One of Rousselet's significant accomplishments is winning the Academy Award for Best Picture for the 2021 American film "CODA," a remake of the 2014 French film "La Famille Bélier" that he also produced.
